aspects.says: An explicit record accessor must be public and return the component's type.
basis: section:A Record's Accessor Is name(), and Overriding It Doesn't Change equals
aspects.reason: javac enforces it, so no wrong solution compiles for a test to catch

aspects.says: Arrays.asList copies nothing: set on the list it returns writes into the array.
basis: section:A Getter That Returns a Date or an Array Hands Out the Field

aspects.says: A method that checks every argument before it assigns any field leaves the object unchanged when it refuses; one that assigns first leaves half a change behind.
basis: section:A Setter Can Check Its Own Value, Not a Rule That Spans Two Fields

aspects.says: A getter that returns a Date or an array field hands the caller the object's own field, private final or not; it returns a copy, or the class stores an immutable type.
basis: section:A Getter That Returns a Date or an Array Hands Out the Field

aspects.says: isX names a JavaBeans getter only when it returns a primitive boolean; Boolean isX() leaves the property without a read method.
basis: section:Tools Find Properties by Method Name, and isX Works Only for a Primitive boolean

aspects.says: A getter whose name after the prefix starts with two capitals, such as getURL, gives a property with that case kept, URL.
basis: section:Tools Find Properties by Method Name, and isX Works Only for a Primitive boolean
aspects.reason: a naming detail the page shows in one run and lists in its reference table; it is looked up, not practised

aspects.says: Bean tools find properties from method names, not fields: a getter with no field behind it is a read-only property, and a setter alone a write-only one.
basis: section:Tools Find Properties by Method Name, and isX Works Only for a Primitive boolean

aspects.says: A record's generated equals, hashCode and toString read the fields, not the accessors, so a value normalised in an overridden accessor makes equal-looking records unequal; normalising in the compact constructor keeps them consistent.
basis: section:A Record's Accessor Is name(), and Overriding It Doesn't Change equals

aspects.says: A record pattern calls the record's accessor, so it sees what an overridden accessor returns while equals compares the fields.
basis: section:A Record's Accessor Is name(), and Overriding It Doesn't Change equals

aspects.says: A record's accessors carry no get prefix, so java.beans.Introspector finds no property in a record.
basis: section:Tools Find Properties by Method Name, and isX Works Only for a Primitive boolean

aspects.says: A JavaBeans setter returns void; a fluent setter that returns this is not a write method, so tools can't set the property.
basis: section:Tools Find Properties by Method Name, and isX Works Only for a Primitive boolean

aspects.says: A setter can compare its value only with the fields as they are now, so a rule over two fields set one at a time refuses some valid changes, and it needs one method that takes both values.
basis: section:A Setter Can Check Its Own Value, Not a Rule That Spans Two Fields
